1zzzzzlll/GrowQuizLauncher.body:
---

## What is this

Kids watch one episode and want another, but parents can't always stay beside them.

**宝贝成长桌面** replaces the Android TV home screen with a small, fast launcher. At the interval you set, it brings a full-screen quiz to the front. Answer wrong and you get a different question to keep going. Answer right and you return to the home screen. All questions are built in and work offline. Volume and back keys can't get you past the cartoons: to keep watching, you must first answer one question correctly.

The same package also works on phones and tablets. There it can serve only as a “scheduled quiz + parental management console” without taking over the home screen. Forced pop-ups at the scheduled time depend on five permissions (overlay, alarms and reminders, unrestricted battery, notifications, full-screen alerts), which you can enable one by one under the device's “Children's Scheduled Quiz → Quiz Assurance.” No computer is needed.

It is based on the open-source launcher [Plume Launcher](https://github.com/aradhyas8/Plume_Launcher) (an ad-free, account-free, analytics-free minimal TV launcher; APK about 0.4 MB). It keeps all of the original launcher's features and adds a children's quiz and parental management module. The 宝贝成长桌面 package itself is about 1.0 MB.

## Core features

| | Feature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| ⏱ | **Scheduled full-screen quiz** | Automatically pops up at the set interval (1 minute to 24 hours), takes over the foreground, and displays full-screen |
| 🔁 | **Wrong answers swap the question, right answers return you home** | A wrong answer only swaps in a different question; there is no “exit” option. After a correct answer, it returns to the home screen and restarts the timer |
| 🧠 | **33,000 offline questions** | Eleven age groups from 5 to 15, 3,000 questions per group, covering 12 categories such as math, Chinese language, science, and history. No internet connection or login required |
| 🗂 | **Multi-select category sampling** | Parents can select multiple categories to define the question pool (e.g., only math and English). If none are selected, all categories are used. The console shows question counts per category by age, and categories with no questions for that age are grayed out and cannot be selected |
| 📥 | **Bulk question bank import** | The console includes an AI question-writing tutorial and prompt templates. Question bank files (JSON) generated in bulk by AI can be uploaded and stored. Each question is validated, duplicates are skipped, and imported questions appear randomly alongside the built-in ones |
| 🛠 | **Question bank maintenance** | The console can filter questions by age, category, and status, and batch disable or enable them. A question answered correctly 5 times is automatically “retired” and no longer appears |
| 🔊 | **Voice reading of questions** | Only questions for ages 10 and under are read aloud. From age 11 on, kids read the screen themselves. Symbols, brackets, fractions, and units are converted into readable words. Options that are a single character, digit, or letter (or a string of English letters) are not read aloud, since reading them would give away the answer |
| ⏳ | **Think before answering** | Options are inactive for a few seconds after a question appears, and a countdown is shown on screen to prevent rapid random tapping. The default is 5 seconds, adjustable from 0 to 60 seconds in the console |
| 😮‍💨 | **Forced rest after consecutive wrong answers** | After 3 wrong answers in a row, rest for 10 minutes. Each additional wrong answer adds another 10 minutes. Restarting the device doesn't get around it. The console can lift it with one click or turn the feature off entirely |
| 🕵️ | **Guess detection** | After rapid consecutive wrong answers followed by rapid correct answers, an extra verification question is added. A wrong answer on verification counts as 3…

# BazaarPlusPlus

**Born out of love** · An in-game mod for [《The Bazaar》](https://www.playthebazaar.com), for Windows, macOS, and Android

[English](https://github.com/BazaarPlusPlus/BazaarPlusPlus/blob/HEAD/README_en.md) · [Official site](https://bazaarplusplus.com) · [Download](https://bazaarplusplus.com/download) · [Tutorial](https://bazaarplusplus.com/tutorial) · [Release Notes](https://github.com/BazaarPlusPlus/BazaarPlusPlus/releases) · [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/cauyxy)

---

BazaarPlusPlus is an open-source project for The Bazaar that does not change game balance. It only adds information and records: a card encyclopedia, ten-win lineup recommendations, match history and battle replays, enchantment / upgrade previews, a battle status bar, and more. The desktop version (Windows, macOS) is a BepInEx mod plus a desktop installer. The Android version is a game APK with BazaarPlusPlus built in, and can be installed directly. The same repository also contains an upload backend, a data analyzer, and the official website.

Regular players should go directly to the [download page](https://bazaarplusplus.com/download) to get the installer or APK. This repository is for developers who want to understand the implementation, submit changes, or build it themselves.

> [!NOTE]
> The project code is mainly led by [Codex](https://openai.com/codex), with collaboration from [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code).

## Quick Start

### Windows and macOS

1. Open [bazaarplusplus.com/download](https://bazaarplusplus.com/download) and choose the Windows `.exe` or macOS `.dmg`.
2. Close the game, then run the installer. When updating, it is recommended to uninstall the old version first, then install the new one.
3. After installation, launch The Bazaar once so BazaarPlusPlus can finish initializing.
4. On the main menu, confirm that the "Card Encyclopedia" button appears and that the version info at the bottom shows `BPP version`. …

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```

Then select iPhone in Xcode and press `Cmd + R` to install.

# MEH VPN

**Minimal V2Ray client for Android; one button, no settings.**

[Download latest version](https://github.com/MEH-VPN/MEH-VPN/releases/latest) · [English summary](#english-summary)

## What is MEH?

MEH is an Android app for connecting to V2Ray that fetches configs itself from several public lists: first its own list ([rzashakeri/v2ray-configs](https://github.com/rzashakeri/v2ray-configs)), then mhcfp and other public lists. It tests the servers and connects to the best options. The user just presses one button.

The connection core is written inside the app itself and does not depend on the Xray or sing-box binary. The only native part of the project is the `tun2socks` engine (a Go library).

## Features

- **One-button connection.** Fetching the server list, testing, and connecting are done automatically.
- **Two-stage test before connecting.** First a quick HTTP probe, then a real HTTPS test on port 443 inside the tunnel (Google, Instagram, X/Twitter, and the Telegram data center). Only healthy servers are selected.
- **Fallback server pool.** Up to 5 diverse servers (by subnet and SNI) are selected. If opening a connection to the active server fails, the app moves on to the next server.
- **Persistent connection.** The search continues until a healthy server is found or all lists have been exhausted;...

# ROS/ROS2 Examples

This repository contains ROS/ROS2 examples covering environment setup, tutorials, people, and vehicles.

## Environment Setup

Run [`serve.bat`](https://github.com/OpenHUTB/ros2/blob/master/serve.bat) (which runs `mkdocs serve`; changes you make must also be checked by running this script and verifying the modified content on [the web page](http://127.0.0.1:8000/)). This opens a browser showing the home page. For details, see [serve.bat](https://github.com/OpenHUTB/.github/blob/master/serve.bat). For documentation writing conventions, see the home page of the [doc](https://github.com/OpenHUTB/doc) repository.

## Notes

* Before submitting a Pull Request, check the following:
    * **Must** use **`mkdocs serve --livereload`** to check that the web page shows the intended changes before submitting
    * The Pull Request title and commit messages must not be arbitrary; they must explain why the change was made, not just what was changed
    * Check that the content under "File changed" on the Pull Request page is the intended change
    * Check whether the Pull Request page shows a red warning (conflicts); if it does, merge the latest repository changes before creating the Pull Request
    * Use screenshots, not photos
    * Do not include personal information, since it is already recorded in the git log commit history
    * Every Pull Request must ensure the whole module can be run directly through the main script; include a demo of the running result in the commit message (animated GIFs can be made with [ScreenToGif](https://github.com/NickeManarin/ScreenToGif)), and provide the runtime environment and run steps in the README.md document
    * When using large models, declare it at the end, and take full responsibility for the submitted content
    * Markdown documents go in the [docs](https://github.com/OpenHUTB/ros2/tree/master/docs) directory and the corresponding module folder; source code (.py, .cpp, etc.) goes in the [src](https://github.com/OpenHUTB/ros2/tree/master/src) directory and the corresponding module folder
    * File names must be entirely in English, with no spaces, Chinese characters, or pinyin; separate multiple words with underscores `_`
    * Files related to each module go in a folder named after the module; each module must support launch, with entry points starting with `main.`, e.g. main.py, main.cpp, main.bat, main.sh, etc.

aaazha686-oss/ktown4u-fansign-tracker.description: Ktown4u Live Sales Tracker for Signing Events (Cloud, GitHub Actions)
aaazha686-oss/ktown4u-fansign-tracker.body:
# Ktown4u Cloud Auto-Scraping (GitHub Actions)

Let GitHub scrape Ktown4u signing-event sales automatically in the cloud, 24 hours a day, and store the data in the repository.
Your computer can be offline. When you have internet access, just open the repository to view or download the full history.

## File Structure (place as-is in the repository)
```
your-repo/
├─ .github/workflows/track.yml   # scheduled task (every 5 minutes)
├─ ktown4u_ci.py                 # scraping script
├─ track_config.json             # config: which events to track
└─ data/                         # auto-generated: track_<event-no>.csv
```

## One-Time Setup (about 5 minutes)

1. **Create a GitHub repository** and choose **Public**.
   > Why public: Actions in public repositories are **free with unlimited usage**. Private repositories get only 2,000 minutes per month, which won't last long.
   > Signing-event sales figures are not sensitive data, so making them public is fine.

2. **Upload these three files** (keep the directory structure above): `.github/workflows/track.yml`, `ktown4u_ci.py`, `track_config.json`.
   - Via the web UI: repository page → Add file → Upload files, then drag the contents of the `cloud/` folder into it.
     (Don't forget the `.github/workflows/track.yml` directory level.)

3. Open the **Actions** tab. If prompted, click **"I understand my workflows, enable them"** to enable them.

4. **Enter the event numbers you want to track**: edit `events` in `track_config.json`, for example:
   ```json
   { "shopNo": 164, "interval": 10, "burstSeconds": 200, "events": [44469917, 44468447] }
   ```
   - To get event numbers, use the local web version `ktown4u_app.py` and click **"Load current event / Search"**.
   - After you commit and save, the next round will start tracking these events.

Done! From then on it **automatically runs one round every 5 minutes**. Within each round it scrapes every 10 seconds, and the data is continuously appended to `data/track_<event-no>.csv` (with columns `time, member, sales, delta`).

## How to View the Data
- Go to the repository **Code → data folder**, then click a CSV to view it directly, or download it.

czg86389-hub/ACP-Ant.body:
# ACP-Ant

Turns Google's official **Antigravity CLI (`agy`)** into a standard LLM interface via the **ACP protocol (Agent Client Protocol)**:
**OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages** formats are all supported, with **tool calling (function calling)**, so agents and applications can connect directly.
Supports **multiple Google accounts used in rotation, with each account using its own proxy node**.

- Uses Google's official command-line program and official protocol. It does not capture packets or reverse-proxy web login credentials.
- Codex CLI, OpenAI SDK, LangChain, Dify, Cline, OpenCode… As long as it supports the OpenAI or Anthropic interface, just enter the address, key, and model name to use it.
- With more accounts, traffic is distributed automatically. If an account runs out of quota, is rate-limited, or requires verification, it automatically switches to the next account.
- **Web control panel**: add accounts, log in to Google, change proxies, view each account's quota, enable or disable accounts, and run automatic inspections. Everything is done by clicking in the web page, with no commands to type.

# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

pht88888888/DSHAPP.description: DSH Android client: runs Node in the built-in Termux environment, runs the DSH engine on Node, and loads the official Web GUI in a WebView
pht88888888/DSHAPP.body:
# DSH for Android

**Run a complete AI coding agent on your Android phone.**

[English](https://github.com/pht88888888/DSHAPP/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) · [Docs](https://github.com/pht88888888/DSHAPP/blob/HEAD/docs/agents/README.md) · [Contributing](https://github.com/pht88888888/DSHAPP/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md)

---

## What is this

DSH for Android moves the [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DeepSeek Harness) desktop engine onto the phone as-is: it runs a Node inside the built-in Termux environment, runs the DSH engine on Node, and then uses a WebView to load DSH's bundled Web GUI.

**It does not draw its own chat UI.** The UI fully reuses the official frontend, and only on narrow screens do built-in plugins provide mobile adaptation. So what you get is not a "cut-down mobile version" but **the same frontend as the desktop app**, just small enough to fit in your pocket.

```
APK
 ├─ Termux bootstrap        bash / dpkg / apt + 64 .so files
 ├─ Node runtime             Termux official arm64 node 26.4.0
 ├─ DSH engine               node_modules, fully unpacked into a private directory
 ├─ Native plugins (self-compiled)  require-builtin / flock / node-pty
 ├─ Web engine (gecko build) GeckoView, does not depend on the system WebView
 └─ Built-in plugins         mobile adaptation / floating ball / UI debugging / logging / memory …
```

## Features

- **Full agent capabilities**: `bash`, file read/write, `grep`/`glob`, and terminal PTY are all available, not just a read-only chat box.
- **Dual web engines**: the `system` build uses the device's built-in WebView (smaller), while the `gecko` build bundles GeckoView (twice as large, but works on older devices and devices where the system WebView has been removed). **Both packages can be installed on the same machine.**
- **Mobile UI adaptation**: the official frontend plus a narrow-screen adaptation plugin, not a separately written interface.
- **Floating ball**: summon it at any time, with customizable appearance, frame animations, and video layers.
- **UI debugging tools**: let the model see the screen and tap buttons itself, enabling end-to-end self-testing.

w3c0929/myscoop.body:
# myscoop

Personal Scoop Bucket repository, collecting Windows software from GitHub, supporting one-click installation and automatic updates.

> **How to configure WeChat Work notifications after forking**
>
> The automatic update workflow pushes exceptions such as `[警告]` / `[错误]` / `[跳过]` from each manifest to a WeChat Work bot. The notification URL is read via a repository Secret, **and is never written into the repository or logs**:
>
> 1. In your forked repository, go to **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**
> 2. Set Name to `WECHAT_WEBHOOK_URL`
> 3. Set Value to your own WeChat Work group bot URL (Group settings → Group bots → Add → Copy Webhook):
>    `https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=你的KEY`
> 4. If this Secret is not configured, the workflow automatically skips pushing notifications and does not affect updates or commits.
>
> ⚠️ Do not write the Webhook key into any file or commit record; GitHub automatically masks Secrets in Actions logs.

## Software Included

> A total of **171** Windows software packages are included, of which **86** reference official releases from third-party projects, and **85** are locally maintained (self-hosted releases).
